content.text:
The pattern looks like a single, slightly distorted perovskite, and the closest candidate is mp-1522319 (BaSrDyWO6). Confidence is low because its cell would have to be contracted by about 2.5% to fit.

- **Peak positions.** The observed peaks sit at about 21.6°, 30.75° (strongest, broad), 44.1/44.45° (doublet), about 55°, about 64.5° and about 73°. These index to a simple perovskite subcell with a ≈ 4.10 Å.
- **Splitting.** The 44° peak is split by about 0.35°. That is too wide to be the Kα1/Kα2 doublet, and its higher-angle component is the stronger one. The 30.75°, 55° and 64–65° peaks are also broad multiplets. Together this points to a non-cubic, distorted perovskite.
- **Missing peaks.** There is no clear peak near 19° (where rock-salt B-site ordering would show) and none near 27° or 24°. The pattern has very few lines overall.

How each candidate compares with a ≈ 4.10 Å:

| Candidate | Pseudocubic or main-peak check | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| mp-1522319 (BaSrDyWO6) | ≈ 4.20–4.23 Å, distorted (triclinic) | Splitting fits; main peak would fall near 29.9° instead of 30.75° |
| mp-1523312 (SrEuCrSbO6) | ≈ 4.01 Å, cubic | Main peak would fall near 31.5°; cubic gives no 44° split; expected ordering peak near 19° is absent |
| mp-1276866 (SrLaFeCoO6) | ≈ 3.91 Å | Main peak near 32.4°; too far |
| mp-1218868 (Sr2GdCu2RuO8) | Strongest peak near 32.6° | Too far |
| mp-1228360 (Ba2InCuO4) | Peaks near 29.9° and 30.25° | Poor |
| mp-18913 (Ba3Cr2O8) | (110) near 30.6° fits | Its 27.1° and 24.1° peaks are absent |
| mp-6144 (Na2La2Ti3O10) | Main peak near 33° | No |
| mp-997098 (CuPtO2) | Peaks near 26.7°, 29.3°, 34° | No |
| mp-18884 (Na4CrO4) | Triclinic, would give many lines | No |

I chose BaSrDyWO6 over SrEuCrSbO6 because only the distorted cell explains the 44° splitting and broad multiplets, even though both are about 2.5% off in lattice size.
